summary.text: In Indian agricultural statistics (Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / ICAR-IIPR), Moong / Green Gram (Vigna radiata) is the fourth most widely cultivated pulse in India, trailing chickpea (chana), pigeonpea (tur), and black gram (urad). India is the world's leading producer and consumer of green gram, contributing roughly 60% to 65% of global output.

protection.name: Mungbean Yellow Mosaic India Virus (MYMIV) (Transmitted by Silverleaf Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Devastating in Kharif & Summer across all belts)
protection.impact: Irregular bright yellow chlorotic patches on young leaves; patches coalesce rapidly, turning the entire canopy brilliant golden-yellow ("Yellow Mosaic"); infected plants become stunted, flowers abort, and pods remain small, deformed, and seedless; causes 50–100% yield collapse if infection occurs before flowering.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot (Cercospora canescens, C. cruenta)
protection.geography: All-India Rainy & Warm Belts (Heavy in Kharif crops)
protection.impact: Small, circular-to-irregular spots with greyish-white centers and dark reddish-brown borders appear on leaves; lesions expand, coalesce, and cause rapid foliar blight; leaves dry up and shed prematurely ("leaf firing"), severely impairing seed filling.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe polygoni)
protection.geography: Late Kharif & Dewy Post-Monsoon Belts (Heavy in South & Coastal)
protection.impact: White, talcum-powder-like fungal patches appear on upper leaf surfaces; rapidly spreads to stems and green pods; leaves turn dull yellow, crinkle, and dry up; pods remain stunted with shriveled seeds.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Spotted Pod Borer (Maruca vitrata) & Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa)
protection.impact:
Maruca: Larvae web together flowers, leaves, and green pods into dense clusters, feeding protected inside.

Helicoverpa: Larvae bore clean, circular holes into green pods, feeding on developing seeds with their bodies partially exposed.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Root Rot & Web Blight (Rhizoctonia solani, Macrophomina phaseolina)
protection.impact: Sunken, dark brown, water-soaked lesions at the root collar and lower stem; plants wilt and collapse; in humid weather, web-like fungal mycelium binds lower leaves to the soil, causing wet foliage decay.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Pulse Beetle / Bruchid (Callosobruchus chinensis, C. maculatus)
protection.impact: Adult females lay small, translucent white, oval eggs stuck to the seed surface; grubs bore inside cotyledons, hollowing out grains and leaving round exit holes; turns stored seed into powdery frass.
protection.passage: Moong — source table 131, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
